topic.title: The Java Language Specification, API, JDK, and IDE
topic.chapter_title: Introduction to Computers, Programs, and Java

sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ready to learn **The Java Language Specification, API, JDK, and IDE**?

Here's what we'll cover:

• Java tools and development environment
• Why this matters for your coding journey
• Hands-on examples you can try

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Think of **The Java Language Specification, API, JDK, and IDE** like building blocks. 

Every great program starts with small, simple pieces. This is one of those essential pieces!

• Start simple, then build up
• Practice makes it click
• Don't worry if it takes time - totally normal!

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: The Java Language Specification defines the syntax and semantics of the Java language
The Java API (Application Programming Interface) provides pre-built classes and methods
The JDK includes the compiler (javac), debugger, and other development tools
An IDE like Eclipse, IntelliJ IDEA, or NetBeans provides code editing, compilation, and debugging
Java SE (Standard Edition) is the core platform for desktop and server applications

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: The Java Language Specification, API, JDK, and IDE - Java tools and development environment. Master basics before advancing. Practice with the examples. Builds foundation for what's next.

questions.question: What does JDK stand for and what does it contain?
options: Java Design Kit - contains design templates
Java Development Kit - contains compiler, JRE, and development tools
Java Debug Kit - contains debugging tools only
Java Data Kit - contains database tools
questions.explanation: JDK stands for Java Development Kit. It includes the Java compiler (javac), the Java Runtime Environment (JRE), and various development tools needed to write and compile Java programs.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an IDE in Java development?
options: It replaces the need for a JDK
It provides a comprehensive environment with editor, compiler, and debugger
It is used only for running programs
It is a type of operating system
questions.explanation: An IDE (Integrated Development Environment) like Eclipse or IntelliJ provides a code editor, compiler integration, debugger, and other tools in one application to make development more efficient.
